summary: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority from City Council to make a final decision. At its meeting of May 2, 2017, Etobicoke York Community Council considered Item EY22.24, recommending that a survey of property owners/occupants be conducted on King George's Drive, between Keele Street and Trethewey Drive to determine community support for a proposed traffic calming plan. This report summarizes the result of the traffic calming poll for owners and occupants of King George's Drive, between Keele Street and Trethewey Drive. Polling ballots were mailed to the affected residents on September 14, 2017 and 33% of the residents on King George's Drive, between Keele Street and Trethewey Drive, responded to the polling. As a result, the minimum response rate of 50% plus 1 votes needed to proceed with the installation was not achieved.
decided: Etobicoke York Community Council: 1. Approved the installation of traffic calming on King George's Drive, between Keele Street and Trethewey Drive. 2. Requested the City Solicitor to prepare a draft by-law for installing two speed humps on King George's Drive, between Keele Street and Trethewey Drive, and that the Drawing EY 17-024 dated March 2017 be amended by removing speed humps fronting No. 3, 1A and 17 King George's Drive. 3. Directed Transportation Services to take the necessary actions to reduce the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h on King George's Drive, between Keele Street and Trethewey Drive.
